title: Who is new Chancellor John Healey? Labour veteran who quit as defence secretary
description: Andy Burnham's decision to appoint John Healey to the crucial role of chancellor of the exchequer was the rarest of things at Westminster - a genuine
body: Andy Burnham's decision to appoint John Healey to the crucial role of chancellor of the exchequer was the rarest of things at Westminster - a genuine surprise.It's not that the 66-year-old lacked experience or credibility - just that he had not been seen as a likely contender, with all the speculation about who would replace Rachel Reeves centring on more high-profile figures.Healey had flown under the radar since his explosive resignation as Sir Keir Starmer's defence secretary in June this year.His assessment of the government's defence investment plan - that it fell "well short of what is required for defence and the country at this dangerous time" - was devastating and undoubtedly hastened Sir Keir's departure from Downing Street.But his resignation letter also included pointed criticism of Reeves's Treasury, which he said had been "unwilling" to "commit the resources that the nation needs to defend the country at this time of rising threats".Now he is in the Treasury hot seat and under pressure to spell out how he will get defence spending up to 3% of national income, at the same time as cutting government borrowing costs and tackling the cost of living.Like his predecessor, he faces the difficult balancing act of keeping Labour MPs happy without spooking the financial markets, while delivering on the government's key priorities.Never the flashiest of politicians, his early speeches as chancellor have been focused on stressing his commitment to fiscal discipline and cutting the welfare bill, as well as banging the drum for Burnham's plan to "reindustrialise" Britain.But he did show his lighter side in a social media video with the prime minister, which saw "Andy and John" bantering about twiglets and scampi fries in the pub., external "I will always stand by my political choices as chancellor, including pork scratchings as the best pub snack,"  he revealed on X.The softly-spoken Yorkshireman has a remarkable record as someone who has been on the Labour frontbench almost continuously since 2001.Born in Wakefield in 1960 and educated at Lady Lumley's Comprehensive School, Pickering, and Peter's School in York, he studied social and political science at Christ's College, Cambridge.Before entering politics, he worked as a journalist, briefly editing Parliament's in-house magazine The House, before becoming a disability rights campaigner and trade union official.He is married and has one son.He first came into Parliament in Tony Blair's landslide general election in 1997 as MP for Wentworth, a former mining area north of Sheffield, which following boundary changes is now Rawmarsh and Conisbrough.He retained the seat with a majority of 6,908 in the 2024 general election, with a Reform UK candidate in second place.In the early 2000s, he held a string of ministerial posts, including housing, local government in the Blair and Gordon Brown governments. He spent five years at Brown's Treasury where he oversaw policies such as the child trust funds and attempts to regenerate and devolve power - the Regional Development Agencies, later scrapped by the coalition government.Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson, Healey said: "The Treasury's a paradox. You have some of the very best and brightest officials in the Treasury, but you have too often a Treasury orthodox that's a dead hand on dynamic government."He added that maintaining financial stability was a key function of the Treasury but "also it can and it has to drive economic growth, raise levels of productivity, support business competition, investment for the for the future".And he claimed the department "was in denial about the commitment that the UK has rightly made to NATO and to our people" to increase defence spending to 3% of GDP, which would not come until 2034/35 under current plans."The Treasury still often sees defence as a drain on public spending and not the driver of economic growth that we've demonstrated in two years," he told Nick Robinson.Healey's other area of expertise is housing. He served as shadow housing secretary when Jeremy Corbyn was Labour leader, despite supporting a failed attempt to oust Corbyn in 2016.When Sir Keir was elected Labour leader in 2020, he made Healey shadow defence secretary, becoming defence secretary when Labour came to power four years later.Healey was a staunch supporter of Ukraine in its war with Russia and made several trips to the country to meet President Zelensky.At his first meeting with Nato allies, in September 2024, he said he was "confident" Labour could honour a commitment to increase defence spending and "make the decisions that allow us to set out a long-term plan to make our forces better equipped to fight and to deter the threats we face".Healey also drove investment in housing for armed forces families, with a £9bn spending plan.Despite his low key style, he proved capable of delivering stern warnings to the UK's enemies.In April this year, he delivered a message to Russian President Vladimir Putin, in a briefing on "covert" operations by Russian submarines, saying: "We see you. "We see your activity over our cables and our pipelines, and you should know that any attempt to damage them will not be tolerated and will have serious consequences."Following the announcement of the defence investment plan, he condemned what he called "Treasury trickery" and the lack of clarity on what new money the Ministry of Defence would get.Healey also made clear that he wanted a clear plan to increase UK defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030.He is not expected to do that in his first Budget, with key spending decisions set to be unveiled next year.But the tax and spending decisions he does announce on 28 October will still have a huge impact on the success or failure of the fledgling Burnham administration.

schema.headline: Who is new Chancellor John Healey? Labour veteran who quit as defence secretary

title: China's families are now supporting more old people than kids
description: Families in China are for the first time supporting more elderly people than children, the country's government has said.Official data released in the
body: Families in China are for the first time supporting more elderly people than children, the country's government has said.Official data released in the last week, external show the ratio of China's dependent elderly people compared to the working age population rose to 23% last year, overtaking the figure for children, which stood at 22%.The numbers are closely watched for signs of how China's shrinking workforce will impact both the world's second largest economy and global growth as a whole.The latest figures mark a significant milestone as China grapples with an ageing population that could have implications for families, pensions and healthcare spending, analysts say.China has been preparing for a growing proportion of elderly people in recent years, while urging younger generations to get married and for couples to have more children.The latest data from China's National Bureau of Statistics show there are now more than 223 million people in China aged 65 and above, accounting for nearly 16% of the country's total population.At the same time there are about 213 million children aged 14 and under.No official commentary was published with the statistics. But Chinese state-controlled news outlet Global Times wrote that the nation's "entry into a moderately ageing society" is the result of a mix of factors, including the "size of past birth cohorts" and longer life expectancy.The shift could place added strain on pension, healthcare and long-term care systems, while also creating opportunities in the so-called silver economy that caters to older consumers, the newspaper said."It reflects a historical trend in demographic development rather than a short-term phenomenon," Global Times quoted one researcher as saying.The demographic shift is "symbolic" and could suggest more public spending will move from families and schools to pensions and healthcare, said Professor Stuart Gietel-Basten from The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.It may also pose a challenge to the country's ambitions, as it could limit its economic growth as well as people's spending power, said National University of Singapore sociology lecturer Mu Zheng.China's ageing population has been driven by a mix of factors, including rapid urbanisation and the effects of the controversial one-child policy, which was in place from 1980 to the end of 2015.The strategy, designed to keep China's rapid population growth under control, is estimated by the country's government to have prevented about 400 million births since it began, though this number has been contested.The policy played a key role in shrinking the population and means there are fewer younger people to support a growing number of elderly relatives, Mu said.But despite easing restrictions on the size of families, Beijing has struggled to persuade couples to have more children, with birth rates hitting historic lows.Other contributing factors include changing gender roles, rising living costs and higher education levels that have put pressure on fertility rates, Mu said.Beijing made further support for older people a part of the measures in its five-year economic blueprint that was announced earlier this year.Financial help for pensioners has been a growing part of Chinese government spending. More than 53 million elderly people were receiving senior citizen allowances and subsidies by the end of 2025, according to official figures.The Global Times noted that many people entering old age who were born between the 1950s and the 1970s have generally higher incomes compared to previous generations, stronger purchasing power and are healthier.The dependency ratio is widely-used to measure ageing populations but it has also been questioned by some experts who argue that its scope is too limited.Gietel-Basten said the use of the statistics risks "taking agency away" from older people - many of whom he says have been misrepresented as dependants.It also does not take into account improvements to healthcare, he added.

schema.headline: China's families are now supporting more old people than kids

title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
description: One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt
body: One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.Another victim, using the pseudoym Isa Brooks, said after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself."I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.Another woman said when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture"."For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so it couldn't be misconstrued.Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence."We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes."How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.During the five-week trial, 11 women - several said they were minors at the time of the assaults - testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them. Prosecutors said the brothers' pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008. They said the three slipped drugs into women's drinks, and "physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop".Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers. Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami. They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family's private security firm, Kent Security.As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

schema.headline: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case

title: Venus Williams: Former world number one loses to Lilli Tagger at Guangzhou Open
description: Williams won six of her Grand Slam singles titles - plus 30 WTA tournaments - before Austria's Tagger was born in February 2008.Tagger's coach Frances
body: Williams won six of her Grand Slam singles titles - plus 30 WTA tournaments - before Austria's Tagger was born in February 2008.Tagger's coach Francesca Schiavone - the Italian former world number four who won the 2010 French Open - is the same age as Williams, and lost all eight meetings with the American during her playing career."When I saw the draw I was super excited and a bit nervous - I respect her a lot," said Tagger, who is 53rd in the world."It is funny she used to play with my coach. I would love to play at this age - I want to congratulate her."While the straight-set scoreline will embolden the critics, Williams did make Tagger - a rising talent who is predicted to have a bright future at the very top - work hard.However, the teenager proved far too good. The 2025 French Open girls' champion was superb on serve - dropping just seven service points and not facing a break point - while handling Williams' pace and crushing groundstrokes off both wings.Tagger broke her illustrious opponent's serve twice - for 1-0 and 5-2 leads - in two almost identical sets.At times, Williams was able to use her powerful serve to get out of trouble - fighting off 12 of 16 break points - and the veteran's trademark competitive spirit never wavered.But it was another example of how far behind the rest of the tour she now is.

schema.headline: Venus Williams: Former world number one loses to Lilli Tagger at Guangzhou Open

title: Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increases
description: The rise in the minimum wage is expected to be announced in the Budget, but 18-to-20 year-olds are set to see lower increases than in previous years,
body: The rise in the minimum wage is expected to be announced in the Budget, but 18-to-20 year-olds are set to see lower increases than in previous years, the BBC understands.Pay for younger workers will rise in line with the increase in minimum pay for employees aged 21 years and over.However, the increase for younger workers is lower than that seen in the previous two years, when Labour raised the rate to meet a manifesto promise that it would remove "discriminatory age bands" with all adults entitled to the same minimum wage.Chancellor John Healey is also announcing measures to give families what he is calling "breathing space" with the cost of living."The manifesto pledge on equalisation still applies but we were always clear it could happen over time," Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds told the BBC: "Of course, you want not just good wages but good work, " he added. "It is a balance of making sure the pressures on the labour market are taken into account."The Times reported that the National Minimum Wage for 18-to-20 year-olds is likely to rise by 3.9% from £10.85 an hour to around £11.27.That is a smaller rise than the 26% increase the Labour government has put in place for younger workers since returning to power in 2024.Even after the reported rise, the rate remains below the National Living Wage for older workers, which is currently £12.71 an hour. It is set to rise by 3.9% to £13.20, the Times said.Andrea Egan, general secretary of the union Unison, said it was "deeply unfair" to keep paying different rates for the same job."Twenty year-old care workers, teaching assistants and security guards do the same work as their older colleagues," she said. "They don't pay less in the supermarket or at the petrol pump. They must be paid equally."The government has also announced a number of measures, including removing import taxes on some food and ending the so-called cliff-edge for those receiving carer's allowance payments.It says removing tariffs from 100 food items could save households up to £21 per year - or 40p a week - when combined with existing tariff suspensions that were introduced in June."We're not going to say it is everything," Reynolds told the BBC, but taken alongside the changes implemented in the summer on goods such as pasta, fruit juice and tuna, he said it would save around £500m a year.Other measures the government announced on Tuesday included:Making permanent a 55p per mile tax-free mileage rate for those driving up to 10,000 miles for work, with the rate rising from 25p per mile to 35p above thatAllowing carers to earn more than an existing earnings limit without losing their entire allowance, replacing it with a taper mechanism instead. However, this will not come in until 2030Giving two weeks of paternity pay to self-employed fathers, who have previously missed out on payments of up to £194 a week for the periodAnd rolling out hundreds of additional Post Office drop boxes to make sending parcels easierSpeaking to the BBC's Newscast, Healey said: "None of this is going to change the world. But if it helps around the margins and its action the government can take, then I want try and fix it."The government will also freeze fuel duty again in the Budget, the BBC understands. The 5p duty discount is also set to continue. That discount was first introduced in 2022, and was due to last 12 months, but has been extended ever since.The list of products the government is removing tariffs on includes:Baked beansGarlicGherkinsChocolate-coated wafers and wafflesBoiled sweetsToffees, caramels and similar sweetsCitrus jams, marmalades and pastesThroat pastilles and cough dropsPlant-based drinks including soya, nut, cereal or seedKeroseneFertilisersThe government said removing tariffs on fertiliser aimed to help farmers, while changes to import levies on kerosene is targeted at households that rely on heating oil.The Treasury said it would publish on Wednesday a full list of the products that will have tariffs removed.A tariff is an import duty paid by domestic businesses buying products from overseas.Asked why the government was making it cheaper to buy goods from abroad rather than cutting business costs for UK firms, Reynolds said: "Where you can make a reduction in the cost of importing goods into the UK, when you think you can balance that with your domestic economic interests, that's a decision we will take."But Balwinder Dhoot, director of sustainability and growth at the Food and Drink Federation (FDF), said: "It's more expensive to make food and drink here in the UK than in many of our close neighbours, as businesses face such high energy costs."The Conservatives said the government's "everyday fixes" had already been wiped out by higher borrowing costs, taxes and inflation.Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said: "Shoppers face rising costs at the till and families are struggling to make ends meet, but Burnham's plan is cheaper gherkins. This is an insult to families hammered by Labour's tax rises."

schema.headline: Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increases

title: Australia vs South Africa: Pat Cummins' tourists fight back to edge first day
description: After a shocking start, a bad call at the toss compounded by a wayward bowling performance across the first two hours, Australia roared back into the
body: After a shocking start, a bad call at the toss compounded by a wayward bowling performance across the first two hours, Australia roared back into the Test in the afternoon.They were helped by some careless South African batting as their happy hookers allowed a position of 203-1 to become 232-6.Aiden Markram, David Bedingham and Wiaan Mulder were all out attempting to take on the short balls – for 78, 50 and nought respectively.On 95, opener Marques Ackerman ran past one from Nathan Lyon with the glory of a first Protea century in his second Test in his sights and captain Temba Bavuma was undone by a straight ball from Lyon. Either side of a knock of 179 last week, Bavuma has got out to off-spin three times in three innings – all for single-figure scores.And while Australia stuck to their task in the afternoon, fielding well and drying up the scoring after 140 runs were leaked at more than four runs per over in the first session, most impressive was the way Mitchell Starc thundered in the day's final moments.At 327-6, South Africa could yet have finished this enthralling day - one fitting of a series decider from which the winner will finish the series on top of the rankings – in the ascendancy.Instead, Starc took four wickets in six deliveries with the new ball, first prising out Ryan Rickelton for 42 and Marco Jansen 52.He targeted pads and stumps, bowled Gerald Coetzee and pinned Kagiso Rabada lbw for ducks. South Africa were 329 all out.Somehow, after everything, if either side is happy, it is Australia.Such is the time difference, many back home missed this fightback, having rolled over when Scott Boland was left out again, Cummins chose to bowl under blue skies and South Africa plundered the bowling through the opening session.When Starc was being slapped and steered for four consecutive fours by Ackerman, few anticipated this finale. Not since Ponting's insertion of England 21 years ago had a 100-run opening partnership been made for a side put into bat by Australia.But Cummins' Australia held firm again where other sides have folded.As a side they remain imperfect. They could yet lose this Test - a result that could have wider repercussions going forward to next year's Ashes.Their batting line-up, with opener Nic Maddinson sent on a flight home after two Tests, Marnus Labuschagne retained despite a run of innings without a century longer than most careers and, crucially, with Steve Smith out injured is flawed.But Australia find a way, often when teetering somewhere near the brink.It is 11 months since knives were sharpening after four sessions of last winter's Ashes series.Batter Usman Khawaja was injured playing golf, the batting line-up weak and the back-ups to an ageing pace attack not up to the mark. They won that Test in two days and took the series 4-1.This could prove an even more impressive reversal at the bottom of Africa.The end result does not prove Cummins was right with his morning decision, however."It feels like there's a bit of moisture in the wicket so we will have first use of it," he said after putting South Africa into bat.Eleven overs later, Lyon was bowling his spin. Not since Shane Warne in 2000 had an Australian spinner been in the attack so early after their captain chose to bowl.Instead, the obvious explanation appears that he made his call to protect a struggling batting line-up.Matt Renshaw will be pushed back up to open, having impressed in the first Test at number five, and Labuschagne given another, possibly final, chance.Batter Josh Inglis, one of the four to come into this Australian XI, has not faced a red ball in a competitive match since March - nor Cameron Green since August.Will a day's play help ease those batters back into this Test, or simply delay the inevitable?Cummins' entry into that unwanted club has been delayed by his bowlers' streetwise nature and ability to sense a moment.Now his batters must ensure he never steps foot inside at all.

schema.headline: Australia vs South Africa: Pat Cummins' tourists fight back to edge first day

title: Fleetwood Town: League Two club fearless for EFL Cup quarter-final after Arsenal upset
description: 'Biggest night in the club's history' for fearless Fleetwood Image source, ShutterstockImage caption, Conor Haughey (right) struck the winning penalty
body: 'Biggest night in the club's history' for fearless Fleetwood Image source, ShutterstockImage caption, Conor Haughey (right) struck the winning penalty for Fleetwood Town against Arsenal to send the club through to the EFL Cup quarter-final for the first timeByJay FreemanBBC Sport EnglandGiven their league positions, form and pedigree there could only have been one winner predicted. Fleetwood played Arsenal on Tuesday with 83 places separating the teams and most home fans arriving in hope rather than any expectation. But remarkably, it was the hosts who booked their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-final thanks to their penalty shootout win over the Gunners.For the Cod Army, who won six promotions in 12 years in their impressive journey from non-league, this result will surely be remembered longest of all. Against the reigning Premier League champions, the club from a small seaside town in Lancashire created history in claiming one of the biggest cup upsets ever.Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts the lead after 21 minutes but, after the break, Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level.And from there, they might have been expected to take charge but Fleetwood remained resolute, prospering from a wasteful performance from Arsenal that included Max Dowman being sent off for kicking out after a robust challenge from Harrison Neal.Fleetwood, who sit 18th in League Two having won just once in their past eight league games, dared to dream and took the game to penalties, with fans spilling on to the pitch in the after Conor Haughey's decisive spot kick."The biggest night in the club's history in terms of opposition coming to town and we've managed to beat the champions," boss Matt Lawlor told Sky Sports in the aftermath of his side's stunning victory."I'm a big football fan and I watch National League all the way through to the Premier League, Championship. So for me it was a tough game to prepare for, but I'm just so glad that the lads have the feeling the way they are and took that performance in to make that town, the club, everyone proud."Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, left-back Jake Batty added: "Our league form's not being as good as what we'd want it to be and for some reason cup competitions everyone gets a bit of a fire in their belly. We just came up with some magical moments and obviously that's one to tell the grandkids, isn't it?""We've struggled. We're not known as a big club in League Two. We get a few thousand fans each game, and just the buzz around the town, you could see the fans in the shootout and all game."That's what we encourage to bring on Saturday. That's what we want on Saturday."Why can't we replicate that and get 5,000 fans behind us every game and, and give us that momentum?"Batty added that on reaching the finals for the first time since their arrival in the English Football League in 2012,  they should be "fearless" and hope for a home tie."It's unbelievable for the town and hopefully we can get someone else at home and do exactly the same thing," he said."I don't think we should be scared of any team."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Matt Lawlor previously had two caretaker spells in charge of Fleetwood Town and initially returned to the club as part of Pete Wild's coaching staff before being appointed on a permanent basis in MarchOn 20 April 2024, Fleetwood's relegation from League One was confirmed, capping off a miserable season for the club on the pitch.That same day, Arsenal beat Wolves 2-0 at Molineux to go top of the Premier League. They would finish that campaign second, but won the title two years later.Meanwhile, Fleetwood have held their heads above water in League Two - and the league is very much in mind for Lawlor, with his side facing Bristol Rovers on Saturday."It's really hard to address the players. I've just said to enjoy it and then we've got a league game on Saturday," he added."I didn't want to be the bearer of the reality, but we've got a game."It was Haughey who ultimately struck the winning penalty to send the hosts through, yet it was goalkeeper Jay Lynch who tipped the shootout in their favour.He pulled off superb saves to deny Ben White, Martin Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes and was left hoarse in the aftermath of a stunning victory at a windy Highbury.It was a victory which he likened to Grimsby's triumph over Manchester United in the competition last season."My voice has gone from organising the defence," he told Sky Sports."We took heart from Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We kind of compared it."It was a typical night in Fleetwood. We were expecting a storm, we knew the conditions would be horrible, so we thought it might go in our favour."It's amazing for the club, the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone."'You question why you follow your team'Fleetwood's win is made all the more impressive when their recent results are taken into consideration.They had conceded six goals in their two games leading into the tie - first from a 4-2 loss away at Cheltenham and then Saturday's long journey down to Exeter, which culminated in a 2-1 defeat."I don't even know my own name right now. My phone is blowing up, and I think I have had about 500 messages in the past half an hour," Fleetwood Town fan Ben said speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live."I have followed this football club for the past 15 years."I was at Exeter on Saturday, I was at Cheltenham last Tuesday night, we were 3-0 down after half an hour, and you question why you follow your team."[This is] not just my best night in football, it's the best night of my life. I can't begin to tell you, how happy and buzzing I am, and how much it means to me to have a moment like that for our little football club on the budget that we have, is absolutely remarkable."

schema.headline: Fleetwood Town: League Two club fearless for EFL Cup quarter-final after Arsenal upset

title: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 on pens): Where does it rank among best cup upsets?
description: Where does Fleetwood beating Arsenal rank in biggest cup upsets?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Fleetwood Town reached the League Cup quarter
body: Where does Fleetwood beating Arsenal rank in biggest cup upsets?Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Fleetwood Town reached the League Cup quarter-finals for the first time by beating ArsenalArsenal suffered a shock Carabao Cup exit at the home of Fleetwood Town, as the League Two side recorded one of the biggest upsets in the competition's history.Mikel Arteta's Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties to a Fleetwood outfit ranked 84 places below them in the English football pyramid.Following Fleetwood's victory, BBC Sport looks at some of the biggest shocks of all-time in the FA Cup and League Cup.This isn't an exhaustive list, and you can leave your thoughts in the comments, rank the historic upsets and share your results.Fleetwood Town celebrated the biggest victory in the club's history as they stunned Champions League finalists Arsenal to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals at Highbury Stadium.The League Two club stunned the visitors when Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave Fleetwood, who sat 19th in English football's fourth tier, a 21st-minute lead.Viktor Gyokeres pulled Arsenal level after the break - but they could not kick-on and were reduced to 10-men in the 86th minute when teenager Max Dowman kicked out following a challenge by Harrison Neal.In the shootout, Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes' spot kick before Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty to spark scenes of ecstasy on the pitch and in the stands.Grimsby 2-2 Man Utd (12-11 on pens, League Cup, 2025)An upset as astonishing for its manner as it was for its proportions. Grimsby Town, a League Two side, beat top-flight Manchester United.Not only did they win, but they were 2-0 up after 30 minutes following goals from Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren.The visitors pulled one back through Bryan Mbeumo with 15 minutes to go and United looked like they might squeeze through when Harry Maguire went on to level in the 89th minute.But an incredible shootout followed, with Clarke Oduor for Grimsby and Matheus Cunha for Manchester United missing the only penalties as each side's 11 took one.The players then went again and, after Darragh Burns scored to make it 12-11, Mbeumo struck his second spot-kick against the crossbar.Plymouth 1-0 Liverpool (FA Cup, 2025)Arne Slot made 10 changes to his Liverpool side after they had won an EFL Cup semi-final in their previous game and the Reds were made to pay.Eight minutes after the interval, the Pilgrims were awarded a penalty after Harvey Elliott's handball and Ryan Hardie drilled home from the spot in emphatic fashion.Hardie almost added a second shortly afterwards when his shot was turned on to the post by Liverpool keeper Caoimhin Kelleher.The bottom club in the Championship held on, with Conor Hazard making crucial late saves, to beat a team who would go on to win the Premier League title.Chelsea 2-4 Bradford City (FA Cup, 2015)Bradford ranked 49 places below their opponents as they travelled to Stamford Bridge to take on Chelsea, who at that point were top of the Premier League.Gary Cahill and Ramires netted to put the hosts 2-0 up and give Chelsea firm control of the fourth-round tie.Bradford had other ideas, though, as Jon Stead pulled one back before Filipe Morais side-footed in an equaliser.Andy Halliday then blasted the Bantams ahead before Mark Yeats slotted a fourth to inflict a crushing defeat on Jose Mourinho's side.Oldham 3-2 Liverpool (FA Cup, 2013)Premier League giants Liverpool had ample strength at Boundary Park, with the likes of Luis Suarez, Raheem Sterling and Daniel Sturridge all starting.League One hosts Oldham were in the midst of financial problems but produced a spirited display against the odds, with Matt Smith nodding in a Youssouf M'Changama cross to open the scoring.Suarez levelled, but Smith soon took advantage of an error from Liverpool goalkeeper Brad Jones before Reece Wabara netted a back-post header to give the Latics a 3-1 lead.Joe Allen volleyed home to pull one back and Liverpool brought on Steven Gerrard, but it was not enough to avoid defeat.Bradford City 1-1 Arsenal (3-2 on pens, League Cup, 2012)A fourth-tier side against Premier League opposition in the quarter-finals of the league cup - Arsenal were clear favourites.Bradford had already caused an upset in the tournament, beating Wigan on penalties in the round before. Up for a fight at home to Arsene Wenger's Gunners, Garry Thompson volleyed the Bantams ahead before Thomas Vermaelen headed home a Santi Cazorla cross with just two minutes of normal time remaining.Just as Mbeumo missed the decisive kick for United against Grimsby after scoring in normal time, the same happened for Vermaelen here as Bradford prevailed 3-2 on spot-kicks.Liverpool 2-2 Northampton (2-4 on pens, League Cup, 2010)Another surprise cup exit for Liverpool.This one happened in the League Cup - at Anfield. Milan Jovanovic fired in an opener for Liverpool but Billy McKay equalised and Michael Jacobs tapped in to give the Cobblers a lead early in extra time.David Ngog scored from a late header to set up the penalty drama, but Northampton were the victors from the spot, with Abdul Osman keeping his cool to slot in the decisive spot-kick.Man Utd 0-3 York City (League Cup, 1995)Ruben Amorim is not the first Manchester United to suffer a shock in the League Cup - even Sir Alex Ferguson has faced the same.The United boss didn't take the game lightly and made just four changes from the league game which they had played three days before, with the likes of David Beckham, Lee Sharpe and Ryan Giggs starting.Paul Barnes, father of Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes, scored twice for Alan Little's visitors, including one from the penalty spot, before Tony Barras headed a third to inflict a crushing defeat at Old Trafford.United put out another strong team at Bootham Crescent for the return leg two weeks later, with Eric Cantona in their squad, but despite getting two goals from Paul Scholes and another from Terry Cooke, the Minstermen went through 4-3 on aggregate thanks to a strike from Scott Jordan.Wrexham 2-1 Arsenal (FA Cup, 1992)Arsenal were reigning Premiership champions and second in the top flight. Wrexham were 24th in the Third Division.The Gunners made the trip to Wales as firm favourites and were just 10 minutes from securing a spot in the fourth round after Alan Smith's first-half opener.But Mickey Thomas sent a 25-yard free kick past David Seaman before Steve Watkin's strike earned victory for Wrexham just two minutes later.Sutton 2-1 Coventry (FA Cup, 1989)Sutton United had a memorable cup run in 2016-17, beating three EFL teams - including Leeds United - before losing to Arsenal in the fifth round.They have also produced one of the biggest shocks of all time.The non-league side took on a Coventry team who were then in the First Division and had won the FA Cup in 1987.The part-time side upset the odds at home, with Matthew Hanlan volleying home the winner just before the hour mark.Hereford 2-1 Newcastle (FA Cup, 1972)Top-flight Newcastle were beaten in the third round of the FA Cup by non-league opposition when they took on Hereford United in 1972.Hereford took the tie to a replay after a 2-2 draw at St James' Park, but Newcastle looked destined to make it to the fourth round thanks to a late goal by Malcolm McDonald in the rematch.However, the non-leaguers had other ideas and Ronnie Radford popped up to score the most famous 30-yard goal in FA Cup history to take the game into extra time.Substitute Ricky George scored the winner - amid scenes of wild celebration at Edgar Street - as Hereford became the first non-league club to defeat a First Division side since 1949.

title: Carabao Cup: Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 pens): Max Dowman sees red as Arsenal dumped out, did Arteta go too far?
description: Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but,  after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal s
body: Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but,  after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal suffered a shock loss to Fleetwood Town, the 16-year-old is facing the first test of his short career. Dowman scored twice as Arsenal beat Ipswich in the previous round of the Carabao Cup and manager Mikel Arteta rewarded him with another start in the last-16 tie at Fleetwood. And this one was perhaps more of a chance than it looked. Arsenal are currently light on options in the wing with Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke all injured. But, after being held by Fleetwood during normal time where the Gunners went behind despite having 26 shots and 78% possession, the Premier League champions lost on penalties following Dowman's red card, after a 1-1 draw in normal time. Arteta gave the youngster a scathing look as he left the pitch and angrily said something to the winger as he went down the tunnel, revealing after the game that it was "something that we discussed already before the match".The young winger reacted to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal and, although he did not fully kick out, he made a movement towards Neal with his leg that gave referee Michael Salisbury a decision to make.It is Dowman's second red card this month after he was also sent off while representing England U19s in the last international break."You have to remember he is 16 years of age, he's a kid," former Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson said on Sky Sports."He wasn't having the greatest of nights so he's going to get frustrated. He gets the chance every now and then to play for Arsenal."He probably feels he should be playing more, he gets the chance tonight, isn't doing too great. It's an old fashioned tackle."If that's Viktor Gyokeres he [Arteta] isn't doing that. That's what I don't like. If it's an exprienced international, I don't think he does that. He's a human being."He's not the last person to get sent off for Arsenal and he's not the first.""When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate. It was very clear." Arteta said following the game. Dowman is one of best young players in Europe and tough treatment from defenders is something Arteta has previously said that Dowman will have to get used to. "For me, I'd put my arm round him, it's still 1-1 and you are in the game." Merson said on Sky Sports. "We all say things in life when you think 'I shouldn't have said that'. For me that's a classic moment where if he could have that back, he'd do it different." Merson said of Arteta's actions. Former Everton midfielder Leon Osman also believes that it was a lack of experience that played into Dowman's red. "It was on the far side of the pitch, but from what we saw [Dowman] can't have any complaints." Osman said on 5Live. "Yes, there were a lot of challenges flying in thick and fast from both teams, and then, there was that moment when a huge challenge came in on him, but as I mentioned earlier they happen so often."And you have to know as a good player, people are going to try to kick you at times, and that's what happened."It was a poor reaction from him and you hope he learns and he learns quickly."The surprising loss to Fleetwood, a team 84 places below Arsenal in the football pyramid, was made even worse by the fact that the Gunners' under-21 team had beaten AFC Wimbledon, a side in a division higher than the hosts, on the same night in the EFL trophy.The first incident of the match came with under two minutes on the clock when the game was stopped for more than eight minutes when a drown was flown above the pitch. Perhaps Arsenal should have taken that as a warning.Arteta named an experimental side and gave a debut to 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill, started 17-year-old Marli Salmon at centre back, 16-year-old Dowman on the wing while goalkeepr Illan Meslier was making his first start for the club too.But the Gunners boss surrounded that inexperience with seasoned internationals such as Jurrien Timber, Piero Hincapie, World Cup winner Martin Zubimendi, Champions League winner Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres.All of those players played a huge part in the Gunners winning the Premier League title last season.However, even after introducing captain Martin Odegaard and £75m signing Bruno Guimaraes from the bench, Arsenal produced a poor performance."First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day." Arteta said of the result."There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. The determination - you could see that was there from the start."Even with 10 men, we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum."The loss in this competition is not the Gunners' first, but it does mean they have not won the League Cup for 33 years.In 2012, Arsenal lost to League Two side Bradford City on penalties and they were also beaten by Championship side Sheffield Wednesday in 2015 at the same stage too.With Dowman now suspended, Saka out for around six weeks, Tzolis working to return and Arteta revealing after the match that Madueke was unavailable with an injury, their options in the wide areas for the match with Liverpool on Sunday are looking slim.

title: Chris Mason: Budget needs to go some way towards delivering PM's promises
description: Two quotes from the chancellor and the prime minister get to the heart of this Budget."The money New Labour had in the 90s is simply not there now… Br
body: Two quotes from the chancellor and the prime minister get to the heart of this Budget."The money New Labour had in the 90s is simply not there now… Britain has it harder now," Chancellor John Healey said last month.And from Andy Burnham, days before he became prime minister: "This change... is the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years."So what happens when the economic realities confront the political ambitions of this new government?As Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS), puts it, external: "We have a relatively new government with seemingly big ambitions but facing a long list of constraints."Some of those constraints… are self imposed, others are being worsened by global events, most noticeably war in the Middle East."Let's be clear, plenty in Westminster in all parties will say that the amount of money around isn't everything – how well taxpayers' money is spent and where it is spent matters too. And spending less and taxing less, plenty argue, should be a priority.But in the bones of many in the Labour Party is an instinct that the government, the state, can and should be a vital agent in driving change and improvements in people's lives – a world-view grounded in a sense that governments should proudly step in, rather than one that believes they should get out of the way.And how do you deliver a proudly proactive state, delivering for people in a noticeable way, when the tax burden is generationally high, the national debt is sky high, energy bills are rising and inflation is higher than expected? In short: it is not easy.But ministers argue all of this doesn't mean the government is powerless.Many are expecting support on the cost of living, and in particular energy bills, to be targeted at the most vulnerable. On the eve of the Budget, Healey said he wants to "start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good".The banks are braced for a levy or surcharge that may pay for this.There will be an announcement about further spending on defence, but not yet how spending 3% of national income on our security will be delivered by 2030 – that will come in next year's Spending Review.And one of the prime minister's key ideas - handing power away from Westminster and closer to you, devolution - will be central too.There will be, the chancellor told BBC Newscast, a "really radical devolution of powers and resources to local leaders that are often better placed to get beyond the departmental systems."But some at Westminster fret extra money for mayors and others in local government are not yet accompanied by adequate checks and balances to ensure that money is well spent.The chancellor will argue the economy is becoming more robust – and yes, there are some economic indicators that are more positive than forecast: growth is better than expected, as is productivity and unemployment is down.But as the Resolution Foundation think tank points out, external: "John Healey's problem is that conflict in the Middle East has once again pushed up energy prices and interest rates."So, despite the signs that the UK economy is becoming more resilient, household and public finances are in for another shock."In essence, we can expect a smaller Budget this time, compared to some in recent years, when it comes to the scale of tax and spending changes.The chancellor has been talking up a desire to offer "breathing space" and "hope" - a tacit acknowledgement that there is a limit to what the government can do given the constraints it faces.It has promised not to raise income tax, national insurance or VAT, a self imposed constraint, as the IFS put it. And there are the international ones beyond its control too.The big question for many will be whether the Budget is – or can be - big enough to meet the moment? Opposition parties will argue it amounts to tinkering.Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith argued the public finances are "on a cliff edge" and wants Healey to use the Budget to "take tough decisions, instead of continuing to kick the can down the road".For the Liberal Democrats, Daisy Cooper warned a "steady as she goes" Budget is "not going to cut it", while Reform UK's Robert Jenrick said the chancellor "can't keep fiddling while the economy burns". Green Party MP Ellie Chowns wanted a "bold" approach but fears it will be "business as usual".The government will try to convince you it is one of many moments in the coming weeks and months that will attempt to deliver the scale of change the prime minister has promised.

schema.headline: Chris Mason: Budget needs to go some way towards delivering PM's promises

title: UK and EU officials to discuss freedom of movement
description: British and European officials will discuss the future options for the UK's relationship with the EU, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has told th
body: British and European officials will discuss the future options for the UK's relationship with the EU, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds has told the BBC.Officials on both sides are expected to begin discussions about a range of options, including free movement, before the EU summit on 20 November.However, Downing Street has insisted the government's current focus is on achieving new deals in areas such as food and youth mobility at the summit.Reynolds said no "assumptions" had been made about what the UK's future relationship with Brussels could look like.Andy Burnham has said he wants an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and EU.But the prime minister has been clear any major changes to the UK-EU relationship would require a mandate at a general election, which is due by 2029.He has vowed to stick by the red lines in Labour's 2024 manifesto, with no return to freedom of movement, the EU single market or customs union, for the duration of this parliamentary session, which will end by 2029.Freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country, is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market.The single market enables goods, services and people to move freely between member states, with countries also applying many common rules and standards.Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Reynolds said current discussions ahead of the summit are around food and drink, electricity and emissions trading.He said: "What the prime minister has also said, quite rightly, is we face a series of policy changes on the European side that will affect us. "We need to get as little uncertainty as possible, we need to have a way to resolve what our long-term relationship will be and he is going to set that out after the summit."He is going to be frank with the British people about what the trade-offs are but no assumptions have been made on that."Pressed on whether UK officials are talking to the EU about freedom of movement Reynolds said: "They will be talking to them about what the future options for our relationship might be."But here and now, the focus should be on the summit and the tangible difference improvements we're going to make."A government spokesperson stressed there were no current discussions on freedom of movement."We are working with the EU on the areas set out and agreed ahead of the UK-EU Summit and within the manifesto red lines," the spokesperson added.Burnham is far more willing to have a public conversation around Brexit than his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, whose government was nervous about reopening a debate that proved so contentious in the past.Some people within the Labour Party had been urging Sir Keir to go further and there is a widely held view that Burnham's comments are likely to go down well with voters tempted by the Liberal Democrats and Greens.But there is nervousness among Labour MPs with small majorities in Brexit-supporting, Reform-facing constituencies.Labour MP Melanie Onn, whose constituency Great Grimsby and Cleethorpes backed leaving the EU, told the Today programme Burnham risked losing trust by talking about going beyond the 2024 manifesto at a future election."I don't think that the scars have healed for many people around the country so I do think this is an unnecessary conversation to be having at this time," she said.Onn, who lost her seat in 2019 to the Conservatives but won it back in 2024, warned against re-opening the conversation, saying: "Trust is incredibly important, it's hard-earned and easily lost, and on this matter I think that we should tread incredibly carefully."Speaking to BBC Wales, Labour MP Ruth Jones said: "We need to be very careful here. We must respect the Brexit referendum result."Asked if a referendum on freedom of movement was something she would support, the MP for Newport West and Islwyn said: "We're a long way from that. Andy Burnham is floating the idea, and it's great to float ideas, but let's talk it through and see what does it mean, because another referendum at this particular time would be divisive."Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told BBC Breakfast that "Andy Burnham has no mandate to be in Brussels, to be negotiating any of this" and called for the prime minister to put his ideas to the public in a general election.On Monday, Burnham left the door open to a potential referendum on freedom of movement with the EU.The prime minister caused some confusion when he told broadcasters that he would not reintroduce free movement without a referendum, but Downing Street later said no decisions had been made on whether a public vote would be needed.Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC on Sunday that no options for the UK's future relationship could be taken off the table.But Burnham did appear to draw some red lines of his own when he told the Sunday Times, external that he would not be in favour of the UK joining the euro or the border-free Schengen zone.The fact the prime minister has not been willing to say the same thing about free movement is being seen in Westminster as evidence that he believes it is a genuine option.

schema.headline: UK and EU officials to discuss freedom of movement

title: Two in court over alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford
description: Two British nationals have appeared in court in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford last month.Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, from Wes
body: Two British nationals have appeared in court in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford last month.Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, from Westminster, London, has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police earlier said they believed to be Iran.  Nouman Essghir, also 24 and from Westminster, has been charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on 22 August - weeks before he was arrested near the airbase in Gloucestershire alongside four other men.The pair appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near the US-operated airbase on 27 September.Dozens of residents were evacuated and a large cordon was put up in the area around the base. No explosive materials were found in the vans by police but a quantity of petrol was seized.The court heard vans bearing the logo "Fuel2You" were spotted close to the base. In the early hours, the vans came across a Ministry of Defence Police cordon and re-routed to another location.Police arrived and arrested five men. They later revealed that one had called 999 and reported what was going on.During the hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court, Essghir stood in the dock wearing a grey sweatshirt and confirmed his name and address.His charge relates to an alleged "reconnaissance mission" on 22 August, around a month before the Fairford incident. Abdulkarim is charged with helping with the plot.He appeared in court in a wheelchair wearing a checked shirt, jeans and a baseball cap. He confirmed his name and address.Both men are charged under the 2023 National Security Act.Essghir has been remanded in custody, while Abdulkarim has been granted bail with conditions including the surrender of his passport.The case will be next heard at the Old Bailey on 20 November.Essghir was one of five men arrested near the base on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and later on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. All five were released on police bail the following day, but Essghir was re-arrested on 20 October.A 25-year-old UK-Iranian national who was also re-arrested on that date on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service has now been released without charge. He remains on police bail after his initial arrest on 1 October on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts.The re-arrests in October led to detectives interviewing Abdulkarim.Eight men have been arrested as part of the counter-terror police investigation.Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the release of the five men on police bail in September had raised significant questions and speculation about the investigation for members of the public.He stressed that tactics used by counter-terror police can appear "illogical" at times but said that "there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them"."In this case, this decision-making has led to swifter progress, better evidence, and ultimately us securing the charges that I've announced today," he added.

schema.headline: Two in court over alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford

title: Bahamas: King Charles acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins
description: King Charles has arrived in the Bahamas for a nine-day tour of the Caribbean - the first time he has visited the region as monarch.The King, wearing s
body: King Charles has arrived in the Bahamas for a nine-day tour of the Caribbean - the first time he has visited the region as monarch.The King, wearing sunglasses and a grey suit, was given a ceremonial welcome at the airport before attending a youth rally.Prior to the trip, Buckingham Palace said the King would not shy away from "colonial legacy" and the impact of the slave trade during the visit but, in line with the UK government position, he will not apologise for Britain's role in the slave trade or offer reparations.Appearing at his first engagement, he told young people it is "only right" to "acknowledge the great suffering and injustices of the past".Upon arriving on the island, he met island's Governor General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt and its Prime Minister Philip Edward, before speaking with members of the Royal Bahamas Defence Force as he inspected a guard of honour on the runway.The King was then met with cheers as he arrived for his first engagement at a youth rally at Clifford Park - where he attended the island's independence celebrations as Prince of Wales in 1973.During his speech, the King acknowledged his 50-year-long commitment to fighting climate change and highlighted the challenges faced by low-lying Caribbean islands, saying that "our world cries out for healing".He went on to call on the young people at the rally to "take up the sacred task to play your part" as "in years to come, this will be surely be the measure of every person - how they answered the call to care for planet earth - the source of our life, our prosperity and our security".Buckingham Palace said opportunities for the King to reflect on the legacy of the slave trade will be built into his schedule in all three countries with visits planned to memorials and other places of reflection and remembrance.A spokesperson for the palace told the BBC that the King's programme on the tour "will primarily focus on shining a light on the many modern partnerships and opportunities for the future", specifically those which are "having a transformative effect on the region". For the King, the spokesperson added, the "tour is both a new journey but also the continuance of a lifelong one, in which he has sought to engage, understand and educate about the most shameful aspects of our past".Those themes will be reflected by the King through the nine-day visit, the palace said.The visit has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda with an emphasis on honouring the past but also looking forward to the ambition and possibility for future generations.The King will move to Guyana later this week where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity. He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where he will be joined by Queen Camilla, for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth.CHOGM is a biennial summit which brings together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.

schema.headline: Bahamas: King Charles acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins

title: Manhunt under way for Tennessee killer Jacob Morley who escaped prison through a fence
description: Morley has been added to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's most wanted list, the TDOC said, and a reward of up to $2,500 (£1,900) is being offer
body: Morley has been added to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's most wanted list, the TDOC said, and a reward of up to $2,500 (£1,900) is being offered for information leading to his arrest. Prison staff confirmed he was "unaccounted for" on Sunday night and begun an emergency headcount and search within the prison, officials said on Monday."The Tennessee Highway Patrol has deployed aviation assets and state troopers to assist with the search," the TDOC said.Prison records show his supervision level was listed as "low" and he was not eligible for release until December 2083.On Tuesday afternoon, investigators said the stolen vehicle had been found in Illinois about 120 miles north of Tiptonville, but Morley was not there. He was sentenced in June 2025 after being convicted of first-degree murder over the death of his colleague Cody Birchfield in 2022. Birchfield's body was found in a metal box under Morley's home, according to Carter County court records reviewed by the BBC.Birchfield died "as a result of a gunshot wound to the back of the head", a pathology report cited in court said. Bullet casings matched a gun found in Morley's house.The pair had developed a friendship while Birchfield was training Morley at the pallet manufacturing company they worked at, Birchfield's sister said in her victim impact statement to the court.Besides murder, Morley was also convicted of vandalism, tampering with evidence, aggravated burglary, and evading arrest. His request for a new trial was denied in May.This is not the first time Morley has led law enforcement officials on a manhunt. His 2022 arrest came after a police chase that crossed state lines into North Carolina.Earlier this month, another prisoner Gregory Redden, 69, who is serving a 15-year sentence for aggravated robbery, escaped from custody but was recaptured shortly after.Convicted murder Christa Pike survived a botched lethal injection in the state in September, leading to the resignation of TDOC Commissioner Frank Strada.

schema.headline: Manhunt under way for Tennessee killer Jacob Morley who escaped prison through a fence
